nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 8:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Source Feed
nodes.notes: Pulls the RSS feed and emits one item per entry (title, link, content). Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Skip Already-Seen Posts
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Keep Top Stories
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 5 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Groq Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: llama-3.3-70b-versatile). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: Groq API key. console.groq.com → API Keys.

nodes.name: Publish to Gmail
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Publish to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#inbox-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm Cross-Post
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Log Published Posts (MySQL)
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Sort Emails Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 100 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats

# Send a weekly summary: Slack & MySQL

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers drip-campaigns work end to end across Slack, MySQL and Gmail.

It moves through 16 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Source Feed
3. Skip Already-Seen Posts
4. Keep Top Stories
5. Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
6. Groq Chat Model
7. Publish to Gmail
8. Publish to Slack
9. Confirm Cross-Post
10. Log Published Posts (MySQL)
11. Sort Emails Newest First
12. Tag Pipeline Metadata
13. Cap Batch Volume
14. Summarize Run Stats
15. Append Audit Row (MySQL)
16. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing drip-campaigns work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Source Feed → Skip Already-Seen Posts → Keep Top Stories → Rewrite for Our Audience (AI) → Groq Chat Model → Publish to Gmail → Publish to Slack → Confirm Cross-Post → Log Published Posts (MySQL) → Sort Emails Newest First → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (MySQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and MySQL aligned by hand for drip campaigns
- Drip campaigns work where "Read Source Feed" is still a manual step before Slack
- Drip campaigns work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and MySQL in step for drip campaigns, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or MySQL are skipped, across all 18 nodes of this drip-campaigns build
- A failed Slack or MySQL call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 18 nodes in this drip-campaigns build
- The drip-campaigns AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 18 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Gmail in the same run, for drip campaigns

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Groq API key; MySQL connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Deduplication is cross-execution, not just within a single run — an RSS feed re-serves the same items on every poll, and without this the same story would get posted again on every scheduled check.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Turn off the AI rewrite step and compare the raw feed text against the rewritten version.
2. Add a second RSS source and merge both into one feed before dedupe.
3. Change 'Keep Top Stories' from 5 to 1 and see how it changes posting cadence.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your drip campaigns process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

**Do not log**
drip-campaigns payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
